sources.entry: Topnotchers - Turns the MacBook notch into a home for Claude Code and Codex sessions as animated mascots, with questions and permission prompts answered from the notch. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/joey-david/topnotchers) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon] ![Native App][Native Icon]

summary.one_liner: Topnotchers is a native macOS menu-bar-style app that shows Claude Code and Codex agent sessions as animated pixel pets around the MacBook notch, letting you answer prompts from the notch.
summary.what_it_does: The app draws a black island using the notch's shape, and shows nothing when no agent is running. Each active agent session gets a small pixel pet beside the notch that animates while the agent works. A pet shows an orange dot when the agent asks a question and a green dot when the task is done. Hovering a pet shows the task and what the agent is currently doing. Questions and permission prompts drop down under the notch so they can be answered without switching to the terminal. Clicking a pet focuses its Ghostty tab, or opens the thread in ChatGPT for Codex sessions started there. The README says it is native AppKit, uses about 42 MB of memory at peak, has no Dock icon, needs no account, and makes no network access.
use_cases: monitor Claude Code sessions from the notch
track Codex agent progress on a MacBook
answer agent permission prompts without switching windows
see which AI coding session is waiting for input
jump back to a Ghostty terminal tab from a session
how_to_run: curl -fsSL | bash (install script; URL not given in README)
notable: Lives in the MacBook notch area, using the notch's own black shape
Per-session pixel pets with orange (asks a question) and green (done) status dots
Answer questions and permission prompts from a dropdown under the notch
Clicking a pet focuses its Ghostty tab or opens the ChatGPT Codex thread
Claims no network access, no account, and no Dock icon
caveats: Requires Apple silicon, macOS 14 or later, and Xcode Command Line Tools
Tab focusing is specific to Ghostty; Codex thread opening is tied to ChatGPT
Install via curl piped to bash requires trust in the script
